key_insight: The paper turns functional gradient descent into a practical algorithm by adaptively improving the representation of the gradient estimate during optimization, while preserving convergence guarantees.
engineering_relevance: It offers a principled way to optimize functions directly with better theoretical stability than fixed-parameter models, which is relevant for regression, PDE solvers, and vision systems.
method: Represent functional gradients with an adaptive, learnable approximation instead of a fixed one.
Incorporate approximation error directly into the convergence analysis.
Prove convergence to stationary points, and to global minimizers under smoothness plus a PL-type condition.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluations on regression, PDE solving, and modern computer vision, where the method consistently outperforms fixed-approximation FGD and neural network baselines in efficiency and accuracy.
watch_item: Performance and guarantees depend on the quality of the adaptive approximation, so implementation choices for representation updates may affect robustness and runtime.
paper_title: Functional Gradient Descent with Adaptive Representations
